steps.text: In a medium skillet over medium heat, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil. Cook shrimp, garlic and white wine for 5 minutes, or until shrimp is pink. Remove shrimp with slotted spoon and set aside.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.
While pasta is cooking, cook tomatoes with remaining 1 tablespoon oil, oregano and basil over medium heat in wine mixture until tender, 10 minutes.
Toss hot pasta with shrimp, tomato sauce and feta. Feta will melt slightly. Serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Shrimp and Feta Cheese Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Shrimp is cooked in garlic and white wine, then tossed with pasta and feta in a fresh tomato sauce.

review.reviewBody: Wonderful mix of flavors! I did make a few changes, though. I used fresh oregano and basil, doubled the amount of tomato, and added MUCH more white wine than the original recipe called for (I used at least 1/2 cup of the wine as the base for the sauce, as others said it was dry). I also added a little bit of salt to the sauce. Instead of just shrimp, I used a seafood mix of shrimp, scallops, and squid and tossed it all with spinach linguini. Definitely a keeper!

Excellent. Made several times for 3 people. Cut the pasta in half, used 2/3 of the spices, oil, and tomatoes. 16 oz shrimp before removing shell. Give a great flavorful balance of pasta and shrimp while remaining lightly sauced. (For exceptionally moist tender shrimp; Step 1: Dry shrimp, salt, wait 30 minutes, place in cold pan, cook at med-high until one side is pink, turn, add wine and garlic, cook until remaining side is pink. Continue with step 2) I always use this method to cook shrimp by itself or for any shrimp dish.

We loved this recipe - so easy and delicious. I used a 2 lb bag of frozen cooked jumbo shrimp, so I sauteed the garlic and the dry spices in olive oil, added a handful of frozen banana peppers (from my garden bounty), and added a cup of Chardonnay. Let that reduce down and added a can of petite diced tomatoes (I had no fresh). Simmered while the pasta was boiling, squeezed a lemon in the pan, added the feta, and then added the cooked shrimp to simmer long enough to get warm. Added a half pound of cooked pasta right into the sauce and ladled in some pasta water to desired consistency. Perfection! Our only bummer was that we didn't make any garlic bread to sop up all that goodness. One thing I'll say for those who said it was bland: TASTE your sauce while you're making it. I ended up adding more spices, salt and pepper as I went until I liked the flavor. It's impossible for any recipe writer to anticipate the quality of spices the reader uses nor their tastes. BRAVO Jessie - I would never have though to add feta - just delightful!

I've been making this recipe for several years now. Ive made it as written, and although tasty, it's just a little dry for my taste. I've since tried other variations based on reviewers suggestions. I've found that a 14.5oz can of diced fire roasted tomatoes, and an 8oz. can of tomato sauce work best. I add a teaspoon of sugar, and I let it simmer until soft. I also used RPCOOKIE's advice to use more white wine. I use a half cup. Also based on another review, if I have it available, will stir in a little cream. Restaurant quality is mentioned in the compliments I receive for this recipe. My satisfaction comes from sitting back, watching and listening to the grunts and groans as my guests inhale this meal. What an awesome recipe to work with! Thank you for sharing!

I loved this dish but I could only give it 4 stars because I made some moderations. First of all, I had the app change the recipe from 5 to 2 servings. I used more shrimp, garlic, oregano, basil, and feta than called for. I also used basil garlic and oregano diced tomatoes and used more than what would have been equivalent to the amount of fresh tomato the recipe called for, which also added more tomato juice since they were canned tomatoes. I also added red pepper flakes when cooking the shrimp. After everything was done I tried it and it was in need of salt and pepper, once I added a good amount, the pasta was delicious!

This was really good! I used a Greek feta that starts with an ‘a’ but can’t remember the full name. Made some minor changes: added an extra tablespoon of white wine, used italian seasoning instead of oregano and basil, 1/2 crushed red pepper, and a full cup of the feta. I also added some salt and pepper. The biggest change was that I used 9 oz of fresh pasta instead of a full pound. 16 oz would’ve been too much, and it also would’ve been too much for the amount of sauce. I also simmered the tomato sauce for an additional 10 minutes in order to reduce it.

Something new to do with shrimp - also very flexible. Four stars because as written there is not enough sauce to go over pasta and it lacks a bit of flavor - I added chopped olives and capers and a bit of salt along with more wine and a bit of chicken stock. Because I wanted to get a few extra veggies into my family, I added about a cup of shredded power greens (baby spinach and kale mix) at the very end, just cooked for a moment til they wilted. Also used far less feta cheese , just an ounce or so per person for the sake of calories. Maybe thats why I found it a little more bland?

I've been making this for years, where I learned it from a Greek restaurant I worked at. The difference is that I carmelize 1 med. thin sliced onion first in olive oil, add 4 large peeled, chopped tomatoes, big splash of wine, 4-5 cloves of minced garlic - let it cook down a bit, add 1 1/2 lbs. peeled & deveined shrimp and then 6 to 8 oz. crumbled feta. Toss noodles into the sauce. Top with a sprinkling of feta. Simple to make and awesome to eat.

I used this recipe as a guideline but I added a bunch of stuff. I used vegetable spaghetti noodles instead of linguini. I grilled diced, red onions and garlic with chives until the onion was translucent before adding the tomato. I eye-balled the herbs and probably used more then what was called for. I also added a dash of sea salt and red pepper flakes with a generous portion of grated Romano Cheese sprinkled on top. I used diced, canned tomatoes because I didn't have fresh tomatoes and I think it worked. I added about a tablespoon of olive oil to the pasta before adding the shrimp and tomato mixture. Next time I think I want to add mushrooms. It was a big win in my house! Delicious!!

I agree with other viewers, to me it was bland as written, for one thing it needs salt (just under 1 teaspoon). I didn't have wine, just used water. It also needed at least double on the basil and a good bit more garlic. I didn't have fresh tomatoes so I used a 16 oz. jar of tomatoes that I canned from our garden this year, and 8 oz. dry angel hair pasta in place of 1 lb. of linguine. The dish was not dry at all and the tomato sauce and cheese blended well. I didn't have feta, I did have crumbled goat cheese with basil (on top of the doubled basil)......YUMMY......The trick is to taste the sauce making sure it is highly seasoned before adding in the pasta, shrimp, and cheese. The seasoning will tone down once the other ingredients are added. Even though I had to tweak this recipe to suit our taste, I still give it 5 stars because everyone has different taste buds and this is a really good recipe. 
My husband and mother-in-law loved it.
Excellent and very easy to make. Agree with those that made extra sauce; used about 2/3 of the recommended pasta but made the full amount of sauce. Would definitely make again.
Cut linguine in half. better yet, use angel hair instead. Increase tomatoes to 3, and add some capers .
I used more white wine and penne pasta and fresh herbs as they were in my green house and substituted diced canned tomato… declared to be my best ever meal by my family members
Only added a bit of pepper to the end result, just cause I like pepper
This is one of our favorite recipes. After making it several times, I increase the tomatoes and only use fresh spices.

This recipe reminded me of the Sicilian Shrimp Scampi appetizer that used to be served at Olive Garden, except it was served with several slices of toasted baguette rather than pasta. I could tell by just reading the recipe that a tablespoon of wine was hardly a taste. I used 1/4 cup and my tomatoes were halved cherry tomatoes. I go light on garlic anyway, so this was fine for me. A little salt, of course.
Followed everyone’s recommendations. I only had 10 ozs of shrimp, so used the servings adjustment tool, it worked beautifully.
I used edamame pasta to keep it healthy, probably not a good move. Edible but not a rave review.
Delicious! I didn’t have olives so I used capers. I think I like it better!
